# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Cardiopulmonary sound recordings often contain heart sounds, lung sounds, sensor contact noise, and environmental artefacts in the same audio signal. This overlap makes it difficult to process the signals accurately using simple filtering or traditional signal processing alone. This report presents a Final Year Project titled Machine Learning-Based System for Cardiopulmonary Sound Separation. The project aims to design and develop a software prototype that accepts mixed cardiopulmonary audio, applies suitable preprocessing, separates the signal into heart sound and lung sound outputs, and evaluates the separation quality using appropriate datasets and metrics.

The report follows an application-based prototype development approach. The literature review examines cardiopulmonary sound characteristics, traditional signal processing methods, machine learning and deep learning methods, available datasets, evaluation metrics, and prototype-related gaps. The report then defines requirements analysis, system design, and an implementation plan for a reusable proof-of-concept software system that demonstrates heart-lung sound separation through audio preprocessing, model-based separation, output management, and planned evaluation. The project does not focus on disease diagnosis or clinical decision-making; its contribution is a structured software workflow for cardiopulmonary sound separation research and experimentation.

# Appendix G: Planned Test Cases and Evaluation Metrics {.unnumbered}

The following planned tests will guide the FYP2 implementation and evaluation phase. Actual results should be recorded only after the prototype has been implemented and tested.

| Test area | Planned check | Expected evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Audio upload | Accept a valid cardiopulmonary audio file. | Successful upload status and saved input metadata. |
| File validation | Reject unsupported file type, missing file, or oversized file. | Clear validation message without processing failure. |
| Preprocessing | Convert audio to the required sampling rate, channel format, and segment length. | Stored preprocessing metadata and consistent model input. |
| Model inference | Run the selected separation method on a valid mixed input. | Generated heart and lung output files. |
| Output review | Allow separated outputs to be played, inspected, or downloaded. | Accessible result view and downloadable audio files. |
| Metric calculation | Compute relevant metrics when reference source signals are available. | Evaluation table containing valid metric values. |
| Error handling | Handle corrupted or invalid audio input safely. | User-facing error message and no corrupted output record. |

: Planned test cases and evaluation checks {#tbl-appendix-planned-tests}

Table @tbl-planned-evaluation-metrics summarizes the evaluation metrics that may be used when suitable reference signals are available.

| Evaluation area | Planned metric or evidence | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Source separation quality | SDR, SI-SDR, SIR, or SAR where reference sources are available. | Measure how well the separated output matches the target source. |
| Noise reduction | SNR or related signal quality indicator. | Check whether preprocessing and separation improve output quality. |
| Audio reconstruction | Correlation, waveform inspection, or spectrogram comparison. | Compare separated output structure with reference or expected patterns. |
| System usability | Task completion feedback and user comments if user testing is approved. | Check whether users can upload, process, and download outputs clearly. |
| Processing reliability | Success and failure records from test cases. | Verify that the prototype handles valid and invalid inputs consistently. |

: Planned evaluation metrics for FYP2 prototype testing {#tbl-planned-evaluation-metrics}

# Appendix H: Full User Requirements Questionnaire {.unnumbered}

The full questionnaire below supports traceability between the Google Form questions and the requirements analysis in Chapter 3. Chapter 3 analyzes 10 main requirement-focused items, while this appendix preserves the full 24-question instrument for reference.

## Section A: Respondent Background

**Q1. What is your age group?**

- Type: Multiple choice
- Required: Yes
- Options: Under 18; 18-25; 26-35; 36 and above

**Q2. What best describes you?**

- Type: Multiple choice
- Required: Yes
- Options: Software Engineering / Computer Science student; AI / Machine Learning student; Biomedical Engineering / Health-related student; Researcher; Lecturer / Supervisor; Other

**Q3. How familiar are you with audio processing or signal processing?**

- Type: Multiple choice
- Required: Yes
- Options: Not familiar; Basic; Intermediate; Advanced

**Q4. Have you worked with biomedical audio before?**

- Type: Multiple choice
- Required: Yes
- Options: Yes; No; Not sure

**Q5. Which type of audio-related task are you most familiar with?**

- Type: Multiple choice

- Type: Linear scale or Likert multiple choice

- Options: Strongly disagree; Disagree; Neutral; Agree; Strongly agree
